claims.context: Selecting model complexity and regularization is a basic problem in supervised regression, particularly when the available data provide limited evidence for departures from a simple relationship. Polynomial regression makes this problem explicit: increasing degree permits curvature, while ridge regularization constrains the fitted coefficients. These choices must be assessed together because the predictive behavior of a polynomial model depends on both its feature representation and its penalty. A higher degree may capture useful structure, but it also introduces coefficients whose estimation depends on the training sample. Regularization can change that behavior, although its effect on held-out prediction cannot be inferred from model complexity alone. We examine these choices on the fixed seed-19 regression task, which supplies 80 training examples and 64 validation examples. The observed training pairs motivate the hypothesis that a degree-one model with weak regularization will perform well. This qualitative assessment does not establish the underlying data-generating function or exclude improvements from curvature. Our objective is therefore empirical and restricted: select polynomial degree and ridge strength using the supplied training and validation splits, while keeping the host's preprocessing and fitting conventions unchanged.
